findings.issue_text: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE in CompatibilityResult.java is silently renumbered from 4 to 3 while 4 is reassigned to FEATURE_DISABLED, breaking external consumers (operator, scripts, CI) that hard-code exit code 4 as 'recreate required'; the operator upgrade code is not updated and the change is not called out as breaking

Operator runtime code does not handle exit code 4 (FEATURE_DISABLED) from the compatibility job, so users with rolling-updates disabled get an opaque failure instead of a clear condition/message on the Keycloak CR status despite docs saying the operator 'will fail'
testFeatureNotEnabled in UpdateCommandDistTest only covers the metadata subcommand; the identical feature guard added to UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() has no negative test

testFeatureNotEnabled asserts only the error message and never asserts the new exit code 4, and no test asserts the renumbered recreate exit code 3, leaving the exit-code contract the operator depends on unverified

adjudication_records.issue_text: Operator runtime code does not handle exit code 4 (FEATURE_DISABLED) from the compatibility job, so users with rolling-updates disabled get an opaque failure instead of a clear condition/message on the Keycloak CR status despite docs saying the operator 'will fail'

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly introduces a new CLI exit code `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` and changes `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3, plus adds CLI-side messaging when `rolling-updates` is not enabled. However, the proposed finding is specifically about *operator runtime code* not handling exit code 4 from the compatibility job and therefore producing an opaque failure/CR status. No operator controller/runtime code that parses these exit codes or sets Keycloak CR status conditions is shown/modified in this diff, so the claim about missing handling/conditions in the operator is not directly verifiable from the provided changes. The diff only updates docs, CLI, and some tests to enable the feature; it does not demonstrate (or refute) operator-side exit-code handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testFeatureNotEnabled in UpdateCommandDistTest only covers the metadata subcommand; the identical feature guard added to UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() has no negative test

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, both UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run() and UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() add the same guard that exits when Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES is disabled. In UpdateCommandDistTest, the new negative test testFeatureNotEnabled is annotated with @Launch({UpdateCompatibility.NAME, UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.NAME}) so it only exercises the metadata subcommand path. There is no analogous test launching UpdateCompatibilityCheck without ENABLE_FEATURE; the existing tests that include UpdateCompatibilityCheck all pass ENABLE_FEATURE. So the feature-disabled behavior for UpdateCompatibilityCheck is not covered by a negative test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testFeatureNotEnabled asserts only the error message and never asserts the new exit code 4, and no test asserts the renumbered recreate exit code 3, leaving the exit-code contract the operator depends on unverified

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, new exit-code behavior is introduced: `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` and `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` is changed from 4 to 3. The new test `testFeatureNotEnabled` only asserts the error text and does not assert the process exit code. Also, across the modified `UpdateCommandDistTest` cases, only the “compatible” path asserts `exitCode() == 0`; no test asserts the new `FEATURE_DISABLED` exit code (4) nor the renumbered recreate exit code (3). This leaves the newly introduced/changed exit-code contract unverified by tests, as the finding states.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UpgradeTest.java setEnabledFeatures(List.of(ROLLING_UPDATES)) unconditionally replaces the whole enabled-features list, discarding features already set on the base test deployment; should append to the existing list

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `createInitialDeployment()` creates/configures a `Keycloak` instance and then calls `kc.getSpec().getFeatureSpec().setEnabledFeatures(List.of(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey()))`, which indeed overwrites whatever list might already be present. However, the diff does not show that the base test deployment already has any enabled features set (the `Keycloak` object is being constructed/configured in this method), so the claimed impact of “discarding features already set on the base test deployment” is not verifiable from the diff. At most, it’s a hypothetical improvement, not a demonstrated defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: update-compatibility.adoc exit-code table lists 3 as 'recreate' and 4 as 'feature disabled' but gives no migration note that the 'recreate' code changed from 4 in the previous release

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the CLI exit code constant `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3 in `CompatibilityResult` and introduces a new exit code `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4`. The docs (`update-compatibility.adoc`) add an explicit new table row for exit code 4 (“feature `rolling-updates` is disabled”) and already contain an exit-code row for 3 describing the recreate-required case. Now that 4 has a new meaning and recreate moved to 3, this is a backward-incompatible behavioral change for anyone scripting against previous exit codes, and the diff does not add any migration note/warning about this change in the docs.
